text:
marta: FYI I opened a perf thread — long-context runs with continuous batching show steady RSS growth and lots of small slab allocs. Seen this across two models (gpt-ish small and a 2B variant).

marta: profile attached (pprof) shows repeated allocations from kv_frag_realloc and a hot path in batch_merge_try_acquire leading to head-of-line blocking. Flamegraph: cluster of samples on kv_slot_acquire -> merge_wait -> attention_kernel_select -> memcpy.

devin: hmm can you paste the CLI you used to collect?

marta: sure:
```
$ ./bin/collect_prof --pid 12345 --duration 60 --type=cpu,alloc
# then pprof -http=localhost:8080 ./server ./profiles/pprof.pb
```

marta: sample log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:02Z] batch: merge nid=42 want=3 got=1 wait_ms=12
[2026-03-15T14:12:02Z] kv: slot_reuse miss slab_alloc=1 bytes=4096
[2026-03-15T14:12:02Z] kernel: picked aten_fused_unfused (lat=1.8ms)
```

olivia: did you try disabling batch merge? we had a theory that low merge thresholds cause frequent split/merge churn when many long-context requests touch different prefixes.

marta: yup — flipping CONT_BATCH_MERGE_THRESHOLD from 3 -> 10 reduced merge attempts by ~6x and lowered alloc churn, but tail latency slightly increased for short requests. also observed KV page thrash when sequence_len > 4k: pages get evicted then re-paged in next request.

devin: that suggests two interacting issues: (1) merge churn causing kv slot ownership contention (HOL blocking), (2) paging/eviction policy not honoring temporal reuse for long contexts.

olivia: can we add a cheap heuristic: if an incoming request's prefix_len > X, prefer no-merge path (i.e., process in its own batch) and mark KV pages as "pinned for duration" of request? pinning will increase mem but avoid re-eviction hotspot.

marta: prototype patch (quick sketch):
```
if (req.prefix_len > PIN_THRESH) {
  req.flags |= NO_MERGE;
  kv_slot_pin(req.kv_range);
}
```

sachin: pinning is ok but we need a backstop: if too many pins, fallback to LRU eviction across pinned tags. Also need to adjust kernel selection: pinned long contexts should pick the streamer kernel not the fused kernel to reduce memcpy. The pprof shows memcpy/reshape cost.

devin: good point. The kernel selector today uses avg_seq_len per model. For these mixed workloads avg_seq_len swings wildly. We should add per-request or per-batch kernel hints so the runtime won't pick a short-seq optimized kernel for a 6k token request.

marta: agreed — added a runtime flag in the prototype to pass req.seq_estimate -> kernel_selector. Changed attention_kernel_select to check req.hint_seq_len if present. That cut attention kernel mis-selection samples by ~80% in tests.

olivia: what about fragmentation? you mentioned small slab allocs earlier. Could continuous batching with small merges cause many tiny KV fragments?

marta: yes. Merge+split causes the allocator to hand out small spans for KV fragments; when splits happen repeatedly those spans become non-contiguous leading to higher fragmentation and GC-like reclaim spikes. pprof heap shows many live objects sized ~3.5k.

sachin: we have two remedial paths: increase slab granularity for KV (e.g., 16k->64k) so merges allocate contiguous regions, or implement a compaction pass that coalesces adjacent KV fragments during low load windows. Compaction might be cheaper than raising baseline memory for most workloads.

devin: compaction needs to be careful with traffic; can't stop-the-world. Maybe a background coalescer that takes ownership of cold fragments and rewrites them into new slots, with epoch-based swap. We'll need careful locking to avoid race with batch_merge_try_acquire.

marta: I sketched a non-blocking copy approach: allocate new slot, memcpy fragments, atomically swap fragment pointer, mark old slot for deferred free. It reduced fragmentation metric in small-scale sim.

olivia: action items?

marta: 1) run experiment that: a) increases merge threshold, b) enables req.hint_seq_len -> kernel selector, c) pins long-prefix requests (with pin cap), d) start background compaction. Compare RSS, tail P99, and tokens/sec.

sachin: 2) add telemetry: export kv_fragmentation_ratio, pin_count, merge_attempts, merge_wait_ms, kernel_misselect_count.

devin: 3) can someone open a PR with the kernel_selector change + unit tests? I can take the compaction prototype and make it safe.

marta: I'll draft the experiment.yaml and run on canary cluster tonight.

infra-bot: Deploy queued: canary/runtime/kv-warmup-experiment -> starts at 2026-03-15T23:00:00Z by marta. :rocket:

olivia: awesome. keep notes on any regressions — if tail P99 increases > 10% rollback.

devin: also remember to test with mixed short+long workloads to ensure we didn't degrade short-request latency.

marta: yep — I'll post results in this thread once runs complete. :+1:
